key_insight: High-dimensional function approximation has a lattice-ball regime with expense scaling as d^(R²)/(R²!), polynomial in dimension d for fixed R, when R² ≪ d.
engineering_relevance: In this regime, spectral approximations can require substantially fewer terms than the conventional R^d hypercube scaling suggests.
method: Approximate analytic or m-times continuously differentiable functions using Fourier, Chebyshev, or Legendre series.
Count spectral indices as lattice points inside a high-dimensional ball.
Identify the second scaling regime arising from discrete lattice-point counting.
evidence_signal: Numerical illustrations cover MNIST digit classification and learning solution operators for Burgers’ and radiative transfer equations.
watch_item: The favorable scaling depends on R² ≪ d and does not establish polynomial cost when R must grow with dimension or accuracy requirements.
paper_title: Second scaling regime in high-dimensional function approximation and curse of dimensionality
